Summary statistics of a cross-validation

Source: R/metrics.R
kcv_metrics.Rd

Summarizes the output of kcv() or kcv_run() (or of gstat::krige.cv(), which has the same columns), overall or per fold.

Usage

kcv_metrics(
  x,
  by_fold = FALSE,
  level = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 0.95),
  by_response = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

Output of kcv() or kcv_run(): a data.frame, an sf object or an sp SpatialPointsDataFrame, with columns residual and var1.var (and fold when by_fold = TRUE).

by_fold

If TRUE, one row per fold (in sort(unique(fold)) order) instead of one overall row.

level

Nominal coverage levels of the prediction intervals, in (0, 1).

by_response

If TRUE (the default) and x has a response column (the output of a cross-validation of several responses), one row per response (in the order of its levels), or per response and fold with by_fold = TRUE. FALSE pools the responses. Ignored without a response column.

Value

A data.frame with columns n, rmse, mae, bias, mean_z, var_z and one coverage_* column per level, preceded by fold when by_fold = TRUE, and by response for several responses.

Details

With residuals \(e_i\) (observed minus predicted), kriging variances \(\sigma_i^2\) and z-scores \(z_i = e_i / \sigma_i\):

  • rmse: \(\sqrt{\mathrm{mean}(e_i^2)}\);

  • mae: \(\mathrm{mean}(|e_i|)\);

  • bias: \(\mathrm{mean}(e_i)\) (positive when the predictions are too low on average);

  • mean_z, var_z: mean and variance of the z-scores, ideally close to 0 and 1. var_z uses the \(n - 1\) denominator of stats::var(), so it is NA for a fold with a single observation;

  • coverage_<100 L> for each level \(L\): the proportion of observations inside the Gaussian prediction interval \(\hat y_i \pm q \sigma_i\), \(q\) = qnorm((1 + L) / 2), i.e. with \(|z_i| \le q\). Well-calibrated variances give coverage close to \(L\). The default levels 50, 80, 90 and 95% probe both the center and the tails of the predictive distribution.

The z-scores are recomputed from the residual and var1.var columns.

See also

kcv(), fold_blocks() and the other fold builders.

Examples

data(meuse, package = "sp")
v <- gstat::vgm(0.59, "Sph", 897, 0.05)
cv <- kcv(log(zinc) ~ 1, ~ x + y, meuse, model = v)
kcv_metrics(cv)
#>     n      rmse       mae          bias       mean_z     var_z coverage_50
#> 1 155 0.3917495 0.2921011 -1.256051e-05 0.0001815253 0.8281059   0.6064516
#>   coverage_80 coverage_90 coverage_95
#> 1   0.8258065   0.9225806   0.9677419

cv5 <- kcv(log(zinc) ~ 1, ~ x + y, meuse, model = v,
  folds = fold_blocks(~ x + y, meuse, blocks = 2))
kcv_metrics(cv5, by_fold = TRUE)
#>   fold  n      rmse       mae          bias     mean_z     var_z coverage_50
#> 1    1 66 0.6304688 0.5340387 -0.1237597885 -0.1662439 0.6162833   0.5606061
#> 2    2 12 0.6730908 0.5421966 -0.0009212365 -0.0179022 1.0958447   0.4166667
#> 3    3 12 0.6107563 0.5330891  0.1781119209  0.2709644 0.9429501   0.2500000
#> 4    4 65 0.6439722 0.5533069 -0.2784011327 -0.3697079 0.5745268   0.4769231
#>   coverage_80 coverage_90 coverage_95
#> 1   0.9090909   0.9848485   1.0000000
#> 2   0.8333333   0.9166667   0.9166667
#> 3   0.8333333   1.0000000   1.0000000
#> 4   0.8923077   0.9692308   1.0000000
